notes: 9 steps: 4 prerequisite, 1 anchor, 4 follow-up. Planned by deepseek-v4-pro:cloud.

steps.title: Learning representations by back-propagating errors
steps.teaches: Fundamentals of training neural networks using backpropagation
steps.why_here: Establishes the basic training procedure for neural networks, which all later regularization methods modify.

steps.title: A Simple Weight Decay Can Improve Generalization
steps.teaches: Regularization via weight decay to reduce overfitting
steps.why_here: Introduces the problem of overfitting and a standard regularization technique, setting the stage for more sophisticated methods like dropout.

steps.title: Bagging Predictors
steps.teaches: Ensemble averaging of multiple models to reduce variance
steps.why_here: Dropout is motivated by model averaging; understanding bagging provides the ensemble perspective needed to see dropout as an implicit ensemble.

steps.title: Extracting and composing robust features with denoising autoencoders
steps.teaches: Injecting noise into inputs to learn robust features
steps.why_here: Shows that stochastic corruption during training can improve generalization, a direct precursor to dropout's random omission of hidden units.

steps.title: Dropout: a simple way to prevent neural networks from overfitting
steps.teaches: Dropout: randomly dropping units during training to prevent co-adaptation
steps.why_here: The definitive paper on dropout, presenting the method, its motivation, and extensive empirical results.

steps.title: Understanding Dropout
steps.teaches: Theoretical analysis of dropout as ensemble averaging and adaptive regularization
steps.why_here: Provides a formal analysis of why dropout works, connecting it to the ensemble and regularization ideas from the prerequisites.

steps.title: Dropout as a Bayesian Approximation: Representing Model Uncertainty in\n Deep Learning
steps.teaches: Dropout as approximate Bayesian inference for uncertainty estimation
steps.why_here: Extends dropout to quantify model uncertainty, a major application beyond regularization.

steps.title: A theoretically grounded application of dropout in recurrent neural networks
steps.teaches: Applying dropout to recurrent neural networks with theoretical grounding
steps.why_here: Shows how to correctly use dropout in RNNs, addressing a limitation of the original method.

steps.title: Concrete Dropout
steps.teaches: Automatic tuning of dropout rates via continuous relaxation
steps.why_here: Improves dropout by learning per-layer dropout rates, reducing the need for manual tuning.

notes: 1 planned step(s) named a paper that could not be found and were dropped rather than substituted: 'How Does Batch Normalization Help Optimization?'
8 steps: 4 prerequisite, 1 anchor, 3 follow-up. Planned by deepseek-v4-pro:cloud.

steps.title: Efficient BackProp
steps.teaches: Practical techniques for training neural networks, including input normalization and centering, which improve convergence.
steps.why_here: Introduces the idea that normalizing inputs helps optimization, a foundational concept for batch normalization.

steps.title: Understanding the difficulty of training deep feedforward neural networks
steps.teaches: The vanishing/exploding gradient problem in deep networks and the importance of proper initialization.
steps.why_here: Explains why deep networks are hard to train, motivating the need for techniques like batch normalization.

steps.title: Improving predictive inference under covariate shift by weighting the log-likelihood function
steps.teaches: Covariate shift, where the input distribution changes between training and test, and its impact on learning.
steps.why_here: Provides the theoretical background for the concept of internal covariate shift, which batch normalization aims to reduce.

steps.title: On the importance of initialization and momentum in deep learning
steps.teaches: The critical role of initialization and optimization choices in training deep networks.
steps.why_here: Further establishes the training difficulties that batch normalization addresses, showing that careful initialization is not enough.

steps.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
steps.teaches: Batch normalization: normalizing layer inputs to reduce internal covariate shift, enabling higher learning rates and less dependence on initialization.
steps.why_here: This is the anchor paper that introduces the topic.

steps.title: Batch Renormalization: Towards Reducing Minibatch Dependence in Batch-Normalized Models
steps.teaches: Batch renormalization, which reduces the dependence on minibatch statistics, making batch norm more robust to small batch sizes.
steps.why_here: Direct extension of batch norm addressing a key limitation.

steps.title: Layer Normalization
steps.teaches: Layer normalization, which normalizes across features instead of batch, suitable for recurrent networks and small batches.
steps.why_here: An alternative normalization method that overcomes batch norm's limitations in certain settings.

steps.title: Weight Normalization: A Simple Reparameterization to Accelerate Training of Deep Neural Networks
steps.teaches: Weight normalization, which reparameterizes weights to decouple length and direction, improving training.
steps.why_here: Another alternative that achieves similar benefits without batch statistics.

notes: 7 steps: 3 prerequisite, 1 anchor, 3 follow-up. Planned by deepseek-v4-pro:cloud.

steps.title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
steps.teaches: Sequence-to-sequence learning with recurrent neural networks, where an encoder compresses the input into a fixed vector and a decoder generates the output.
steps.why_here: Introduces the encoder-decoder framework for sequence transduction, which the Transformer later replaces the recurrent components of.

steps.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
steps.teaches: Attention mechanism that allows the decoder to focus on relevant parts of the input sequence, avoiding the fixed-vector bottleneck.
steps.why_here: Introduces attention, the core idea that the Transformer extends to self-attention across the entire sequence.

steps.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Generic Convolutional and Recurrent Networks for Sequence Modeling
steps.teaches: Non-recurrent sequence modeling using convolutional networks and positional embeddings, showing that recurrence is not necessary for sequence tasks.
steps.why_here: Demonstrates a fully parallelizable sequence model with positional information, directly motivating the Transformer's design.

steps.title: Is Space-Time Attention All You Need for Video Understanding?
steps.teaches: The Transformer architecture: multi-head self-attention, positional encoding, and feed-forward layers, entirely without recurrence or convolution.
steps.why_here: This is the paper that defines the Transformer, the topic the learner asked about.

steps.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
steps.teaches: Pre-training a deep bidirectional Transformer on large text corpora and fine-tuning for downstream tasks, establishing the dominant NLP paradigm.
steps.why_here: Shows how the Transformer encoder can be pre-trained to capture rich contextual representations, leading to state-of-the-art results across NLP.

steps.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
steps.teaches: Applying a pure Transformer encoder to image patches, demonstrating that the architecture generalizes beyond text to vision.
steps.why_here: Extends the Transformer to computer vision, proving its versatility and sparking the ViT line of research.

steps.title: Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models beyond a Fixed-Length Context
steps.teaches: Introducing recurrence into Transformers to handle longer contexts by caching hidden states, overcoming the fixed-length limitation.
steps.why_here: Addresses a key limitation of the original Transformer (fixed context window) and enables modeling of long-range dependencies.

notes: 9 steps: 2 prerequisite, 1 anchor, 6 follow-up. Planned by deepseek-v4-pro:cloud.

steps.title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
steps.teaches: Variational inference and the reparameterization trick for training latent variable models.
steps.why_here: Diffusion models are trained by optimizing a variational lower bound, so understanding variational inference is essential before seeing how it is applied to diffusion processes.

steps.title: Deep Unsupervised Learning using Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics
steps.teaches: The original formulation of diffusion models as a reverse diffusion process trained with a variational bound.
steps.why_here: This paper introduces the core idea of gradually destroying and then reconstructing data, which is the foundation that the anchor paper simplifies and scales.

steps.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
steps.teaches: The modern denoising diffusion probabilistic model with a simplified training objective and high-quality image generation.
steps.why_here: This is the anchor paper that made diffusion models practical and popular; it builds directly on the variational bound from step 1 and the diffusion process from step 2.

steps.title: Generative Modeling by Estimating Gradients of the Data Distribution
steps.teaches: Estimating the score (gradient of the log-density) and sampling with Langevin dynamics as an alternative generative approach.
steps.why_here: This parallel line of work is introduced after the anchor to show a different perspective that will later be unified with diffusion models.

steps.title: Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations
steps.teaches: A continuous-time framework that unifies diffusion models and score-based models through stochastic differential equations.
steps.why_here: Having seen both DDPM and score-based models, this paper provides the theoretical connection and generalizes both.

steps.title: Improved Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
steps.teaches: Practical improvements to DDPM, including learned variances and a cosine noise schedule.
steps.why_here: This follow-up refines the anchor, showing how to achieve better likelihoods and sample quality.

steps.title: Diffusion Models Beat GANs on Image Synthesis
steps.teaches: Scaling up diffusion models with classifier guidance to surpass GANs on image synthesis.
steps.why_here: This paper demonstrates the competitiveness of diffusion models, building on the improvements from step 6.

steps.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
steps.teaches: Applying diffusion in a learned latent space to enable high-resolution image synthesis efficiently.
steps.why_here: This follow-up addresses the computational cost of pixel-space diffusion, using the VAE idea from step 1 to compress data before diffusing.

steps.title: Elucidating the Design Space of Diffusion-Based Generative Models
steps.teaches: A systematic analysis of diffusion model design choices, leading to state-of-the-art sampling speed and quality.
steps.why_here: This paper consolidates the lessons from previous steps and provides a modern best-practice recipe.

notes: 9 steps: 3 prerequisite, 1 anchor, 5 follow-up. Planned by deepseek-v4-pro:cloud.

steps.title: A Fast Learning Algorithm for Deep Belief Nets
steps.teaches: Deep generative models and unsupervised learning via layer-wise pretraining of restricted Boltzmann machines.
steps.why_here: Introduces the idea of learning a generative model of data using neural networks, which is the foundation for all generative models including GANs. It establishes the deep learning paradigm that GANs later build upon.

steps.title: Noise-contrastive estimation: A new estimation principle for unnormalized statistical models
steps.teaches: Training a model by contrasting data samples with noise samples, using a logistic regression classifier to estimate density ratios.
steps.why_here: Presents the core idea of training a model to distinguish real data from generated noise, which is a direct precursor to the adversarial training framework of GANs. It provides the statistical estimation principle that GANs generalize.

steps.title: ImageNet classification with deep convolutional neural networks
steps.teaches: Deep convolutional neural networks for large-scale image classification, demonstrating the power of CNNs for visual data.
steps.why_here: Provides the architectural foundation (CNNs) that later GAN variants like DCGAN use for image generation. Understanding CNNs is necessary to follow the followup papers that apply GANs to images.

steps.title: Conditional Generative Adversarial Nets
steps.teaches: The GAN framework: a generator and discriminator play a minimax game, where the generator learns to produce samples indistinguishable from real data.
steps.why_here: This is the anchor paper that introduces generative adversarial networks. It builds on the previous ideas of generative modeling, noise-contrastive estimation, and deep learning to propose a novel adversarial training procedure.

steps.title: Unsupervised Representation Learning with Deep Convolutional Generative\n Adversarial Networks
steps.teaches: Applying convolutional architectures to GANs (DCGAN) to improve image generation quality and stability, and showing the learned representations are useful for downstream tasks.
steps.why_here: Extends the GAN framework to image data by using CNNs, addressing the instability of the original GAN on images. It relies on the CNN knowledge from step 3 and the GAN framework from step 4.

steps.title: Improved Techniques for Training GANs
steps.teaches: A set of practical techniques (feature matching, minibatch discrimination, historical averaging, etc.) to stabilize GAN training and improve sample quality.
steps.why_here: Addresses the training difficulties of GANs identified in the anchor paper. It provides empirical solutions that are widely used, and it sets the stage for later theoretical analyses.

steps.title: Wasserstein GAN
steps.teaches: Wasserstein distance as a more meaningful loss metric for GANs, leading to more stable training and better correlation with sample quality.
steps.why_here: Provides a theoretical grounding for GAN training by replacing the Jensen-Shannon divergence with the Wasserstein distance. It explains why the original GAN training is unstable and offers a principled alternative, building on the empirical observations from step 6.

steps.title: Progressive Growing of GANs for Improved Quality, Stability, and\n Variation
steps.teaches: Progressive training of GANs, starting from low-resolution images and gradually increasing resolution, to generate high-quality, high-resolution images.
steps.why_here: Builds on the stability improvements from steps 6 and 7 to enable generation of high-resolution images. It introduces a training curriculum that is now standard for high-quality image synthesis.

steps.title: A Style-Based Generator Architecture for Generative Adversarial Networks
steps.teaches: Style-based generator architecture that separates high-level attributes from stochastic variation, enabling control over the generated image style and improving quality.
steps.why_here: Represents a major architectural advance in GANs, building on the progressive growing approach from step 8. It introduces the style-based generator that has become the basis for state-of-the-art image generation.

notes: 9 steps: 3 prerequisite, 1 anchor, 5 follow-up. Planned by deepseek-v4-pro:cloud.

steps.title: Indexing by latent semantic analysis
steps.teaches: Words can be represented as vectors in a reduced-dimensional space derived from co-occurrence statistics, capturing semantic similarity.
steps.why_here: Introduces the foundational idea of representing word meaning as vectors in a continuous space, which all later embedding methods build upon.

steps.title: A neural probabilistic language model
steps.teaches: Neural networks can learn distributed representations of words as part of a language model, where similar words get similar vectors.
steps.why_here: Shows that word representations can be learned automatically from data using neural networks, a direct precursor to word2vec's training approach.

steps.title: Natural Language Processing (almost) from Scratch
steps.teaches: Pre-trained word embeddings can be used as features to improve performance across many NLP tasks, demonstrating their general utility.
steps.why_here: Establishes the practical value of learned word representations for downstream tasks, motivating the need for efficient training methods like word2vec.

steps.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
steps.teaches: Efficient training of word embeddings using simple neural architectures (CBOW and skip-gram) on large corpora, producing vectors that capture rich semantic and syntactic relationships.
steps.why_here: This is the anchor paper that introduced word2vec, the method that popularized word embeddings and is the central topic of this sequence.

steps.title: Glove: Global Vectors for Word Representation
steps.teaches: Word embeddings can also be obtained by factorizing a global word-word co-occurrence matrix, offering an alternative to local context prediction.
steps.why_here: Presents a competing approach to word2vec that uses global statistics, showing that the core idea can be implemented differently and sparking comparisons.

steps.title: Improving Distributional Similarity with Lessons Learned from Word Embeddings
steps.teaches: The success of word2vec can be explained by its connection to traditional distributional similarity methods, and hyperparameters play a crucial role.
steps.why_here: Analyzes why word2vec works, linking it back to earlier distributional semantics and providing practical guidance, deepening understanding of the anchor method.

steps.title: Enriching Word Vectors with Subword Information
steps.teaches: Word embeddings can be improved by incorporating subword information (character n-grams), which helps with rare words and morphology.
steps.why_here: Extends word2vec to handle subword units, addressing a limitation of the original method and showing how embeddings can be enhanced.

steps.title: Deep Contextualized Word Representations
steps.teaches: Word representations can be contextual, meaning the vector for a word depends on its surrounding sentence, capturing polysemy and context-specific meaning.
steps.why_here: Introduces a major shift from static embeddings to contextual ones, building on the idea of learned representations but making them dynamic.

steps.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
steps.teaches: Large-scale pre-training of deep bidirectional transformers produces highly effective contextual embeddings that can be fine-tuned for many tasks, becoming the new standard.
steps.why_here: Represents the culmination of the contextual embedding trend, showing how the ideas from word2vec evolved into powerful pre-trained language models.

notes: 7 steps: 3 prerequisite, 1 anchor, 3 follow-up. Planned by deepseek-v4-pro:cloud.
2 of 6 consecutive steps go backwards in time by more than two years — the sequence may be ordered by topic rather than by dependency.

steps.title: Receptive fields, binocular interaction and functional architecture in the cat's visual cortex
steps.teaches: Biological visual cortex uses local receptive fields and hierarchical processing, inspiring local connectivity in artificial networks.
steps.why_here: Provides the biological motivation for local connectivity and hierarchical feature extraction, which are core to CNNs; this is the foundational idea from neuroscience that CNNs build upon.

steps.title: Learning representations by back-propagating errors
steps.teaches: Backpropagation algorithm for training multi-layer neural networks by gradient descent.
steps.why_here: CNNs are trained with backpropagation; this paper introduces the learning algorithm that makes training deep networks possible, a necessary tool before any convolutional architecture can be learned.

steps.title: Neocognitron: A self-organizing neural network model for a mechanism of pattern recognition unaffected by shift in position
steps.teaches: Neocognitron: an early neural network with local receptive fields and weight sharing, robust to shifts in position.
steps.why_here: Translates the biological idea into a computational model with convolutional-like layers and weight sharing, directly preceding the modern CNN; it shows how local connectivity and shared weights can be implemented in a trainable network (though trained differently).

steps.title: Gradient-based learning applied to document recognition
steps.teaches: Convolutional neural networks (LeNet-5) trained by backpropagation for document recognition, combining local receptive fields, weight sharing, and subsampling.
steps.why_here: This is the anchor paper that defines the modern CNN: it integrates the prerequisites (local connectivity from Hubel & Wiesel, backprop from Rumelhart, and the neocognitron's architecture) into a practical, end-to-end trainable system, establishing the standard CNN architecture.

steps.title: ImageNet classification with deep convolutional neural networks
steps.teaches: Deep CNNs (AlexNet) with ReLU activations, dropout, and GPU training achieve breakthrough performance on large-scale image classification.
steps.why_here: Shows that scaling up the CNN architecture from LeNet with more layers, data, and compute leads to dramatic improvements, reigniting interest in deep learning; it builds directly on the anchor's architecture but demonstrates its power on a much larger problem.

steps.title: Visualizing and Understanding Convolutional Networks
steps.teaches: Visualization techniques (deconvolutional networks) reveal what features CNNs learn at each layer, aiding understanding and architecture improvement.
steps.why_here: After seeing the success of AlexNet, this paper provides insight into why deep CNNs work by visualizing learned features, which helps diagnose and improve architectures; it is a natural followup to understand the internal representations of the deep network introduced in the previous step.

steps.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
steps.teaches: Residual connections (skip connections) enable training of very deep networks (ResNet) by addressing degradation, achieving state-of-the-art results.
steps.why_here: Building on the understanding from visualization and the trend toward deeper networks, this paper introduces a key architectural innovation that allows training hundreds of layers, overcoming limitations of plain deep CNNs; it represents a major extension of the CNN paradigm.

steps.title: Policy Gradient Methods for Reinforcement Learning with Function Approximation
steps.teaches: Fundamentals of policy optimization in reinforcement learning, including the policy gradient theorem.
steps.why_here: RLHF optimizes a policy using gradient-based methods; this paper provides the necessary RL foundation.

steps.title: Inverse Reinforcement Learning algorithms and features for robot navigation in crowds: An experimental comparison
steps.teaches: Learning a reward function from observed behavior, a precursor to learning from human feedback.
steps.why_here: RLHF learns a reward model from human preferences, which is conceptually similar to IRL; this paper introduces the idea of inferring rewards from external signals.

steps.title: Preference-based reinforcement learning: a formal framework and a policy iteration algorithm
steps.teaches: Formalizing RL with preferences instead of numerical rewards, and an algorithm for policy iteration.
steps.why_here: This is the direct precursor to deep RLHF, establishing the framework of learning from pairwise preferences.

notes: 9 steps: 4 prerequisite, 1 anchor, 4 follow-up. Planned by deepseek-v4-pro:cloud.

steps.title: Neural Networks and the Bias/Variance Dilemma
steps.teaches: Bias-variance tradeoff and overfitting
steps.why_here: Establishes the bias-variance tradeoff, the core reason regularization is needed; no prior knowledge assumed.

steps.title: INADMISSIBILITY OF THE USUAL ESTIMATOR FOR THE MEAN OF A MULTIVARIATE NORMAL DISTRIBUTION
steps.teaches: Shrinkage can improve estimation
steps.why_here: Shows that shrinking estimates toward a common value can reduce total error, providing theoretical motivation for penalization introduced next.

steps.title: Ridge Regression: Biased Estimation for Nonorthogonal Problems
steps.teaches: L2 penalty in linear regression
steps.why_here: Applies shrinkage via an L2 penalty to linear regression, giving the first widely used regularization technique.

steps.title: A Practical Bayesian Framework for Backpropagation Networks
steps.teaches: Regularization as Bayesian prior
steps.why_here: Connects regularization to Bayesian priors, showing weight decay as maximum a posteriori estimation, which deepens understanding before sparse penalties.

steps.title: Regression Shrinkage and Selection Via the Lasso
steps.teaches: L1 penalty and variable selection
steps.why_here: Introduces L1 regularization, the anchor method that extends shrinkage to variable selection and defines modern regularization.

steps.title: Least angle regression
steps.teaches: Efficient algorithm for lasso
steps.why_here: Provides an efficient algorithm for computing lasso solutions, making the anchor method practical for larger problems.

steps.title: Regularization and Variable Selection Via the Elastic Net
steps.teaches: Combining L1 and L2 penalties
steps.why_here: Combines L1 and L2 penalties to address lasso limitations with correlated features, a direct extension of the anchor.

steps.title: Dropout: a simple way to prevent neural networks from overfitting
steps.teaches: Stochastic regularization for neural networks
steps.why_here: Transfers regularization to neural networks via stochastic noise injection, showing how the idea generalizes beyond linear models.

steps.title: Understanding deep learning requires rethinking generalization
steps.teaches: Implicit regularization in deep learning
steps.why_here: Challenges classical bias-variance explanations for deep networks, pointing to implicit regularization and motivating current research.

steps.title: Noise-contrastive estimation: A new estimation principle for unnormalized statistical models
